answer: A public random beacon — a zephyr no one can predict — picks a few identities each epoch for a live spot-audit: each chosen agent must complete a fresh piece of verifiable work tied to its own ivory ledger of past deeds, inside a short window. A farm cannot staff a thousand fakes at once or guess which will be called, so every extra identity needs a live worker on standby plus a bond that burns on a missed audit. Honest agents pass because they are actually present; shells whisper excuses and lose their standing.
